scenes.headline: How a lidar keeps a Gaussian splat's walls flat
scenes.sub: Hesai's handheld scanner, from laser pulse to splat
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Parallax! Hesai makes lidar for cars. Now it sells a handheld that turns a room into a Gaussian splat.

scenes.text: Photos alone cannot tell where a blank wall is. Lidar measures it, gives every camera its pose, and holds each Gaussian on the surface while training.
scenes.mark: holds each Gaussian on the surface
scenes.say: Photos alone cannot tell where a blank wall is. The lidar measures it, poses every camera, and holds each Gaussian on the surface.

scenes.title: One point from one pulse

parts.say: Fire a short pulse and time the echo.
Half the round trip at the speed of light is the range.

parts.note: noisy per shot, so average many
parts.say: One shot is noisy. Millimetres come from averaging many shots.

scenes.say: A time of flight lidar measures one point at a time.

scenes.title: From a walk to a splat

steps.say: The stick carries a lidar, fisheye cameras and an inertial unit, synchronised to the microsecond.
The inertial unit predicts motion between sweeps, so each sweep is deskewed and registered against the map.
That trajectory gives every camera its pose, and the points land in one metric frame.
Training starts from the lidar points and compares rendered depth with the laser's.

scenes.label: mean point spacing over a 15-minute room scan
scenes.note: 569,000 points a second on 312 square metres
scenes.say: Over a fifteen minute scan of a hundred square metre room, points sit under a millimetre apart. Density is not the bottleneck.

left.title: Appearance only
items: Blank walls drift off the plane
left.say: Fit appearance alone and a blank wall drifts off its plane. Training longer lets it wander further.

right.title: Plus a lidar depth term
items: Walls stay flat as training runs
right.say: Compare rendered depth with the laser's, and the wall stays flat.

scenes.credit: Pixar RenderMan tutorial, scan made with Kosmo

steps.say: This is Pixar's plaza, scanned with an early unit and rendered in RenderMan.
Most of its splats are thin, opaque discs lying on surfaces, a few millimetres across.

scenes.text: Point rate is not the question. Drift over a building, and whether lidar depth enters the loss, are.
scenes.mark: whether lidar depth enters the loss
scenes.say: So point rate is not the question. Drift over a building, and whether lidar depth enters the loss, are.

recap: Time the echo, average the shots
Lidar and IMU give the poses
A depth term keeps walls flat
scenes.say: Time the echo and average. Lidar and inertia give the poses. A depth term keeps the walls flat.
